note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden-onset, left-sided headache started this morning with dizziness, blurred vision (zigzag lines), and nausea/vomiting. Pain described as severe but patient rates current pain around 5–6/10. Worsens with movement; started suddenly and is persistent.
- Onset, duration, progression: Headache began this morning, progressed to current level; paracetamol/acetaminophen taken about 3 hours ago without relief.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea with two episodes of vomiting; blurry vision with visual phenomena; dizziness; no reported weakness or gait disturbance.
- Past medical history: Kidney stones.
- Medications: No regular medications. Took acetaminophen (paracetamol) for headache; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Not known/denied by patient.
- Social history: Not documented.
- Family history: Mother with migraines; mother has hypothyroidism (family history of thyroid disease and migraines).
- Pregnancy status: Pregnancy unlikely per patient.
- Additional notes: Patient expresses significant concern about serious conditions (e.g., brain tumor or stroke). No focal neurological deficits reported by patient at this time.

Objective:
- General/neurologic exam: No focal neurological deficits described; patient reports dizziness and one-sided headache with visual disturbances but walking described as normal; no weakness or ataxia noted.
- Eyes/vision: Blurred vision with zigzag visual phenomena.
- Headache characteristics: Left-sided head pain; movement aggravates symptoms.
- GI: Nausea and vomiting (two episodes).
- Other: No vitals or laboratory data recorded in transcript; no imaging results available.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Migraine (likely migraine with aura given unilateral head pain, visual disturbances, nausea/vomiting)
   - Differential diagnoses: Stroke or intracranial pathology less likely given normal gait and absence of focal deficits (patient worried about these). Migraine with aura remains most likely.
   - Investigations planned: Full neurological examination if symptoms persist or worsen; no imaging ordered at this time.
   - Treatment planned: 
     - Ibuprofen (NSAID) with antiemetic as needed.
     - Hydration with sugary, carbonated beverage (e.g., Coca-Cola) as part of initial management.
     - If symptoms persist or worsen, escalation to migraine-specific relief medication as advised.
   - Referrals: None at this time; plan to re-evaluate at scheduled appointment for a more thorough neurological assessment.
   - Follow-up: Schedule or arrange an assessment later today; if symptoms improve significantly, cancellation of the planned assessment is possible.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, etc.) not documented.
  - Complete medication reconciliation beyond paracetamol; no other regular meds listed.
  - No formal neurological exam documented in this visit (only patient-reported status).
  - No imaging results or formal headache red-flag screen documented.
  - Social history (smoking, alcohol, occupation) not provided.
- Internal conflicts: None identified in the transcript.
- Transcript quality: Some interruptions/loss of connection noted; overall coherent with patient-reported symptoms and physician’s interpretation. No conflicting statements about the diagnosis.
